what_this_is: A DEBT SNAPSHOT, not a target and not an approval. It records which test node ids were already failing so REQ-HARNESS-5920's node-id delta can tell a NEW regression from pre-existing debt. Recording a failure here does not bless it.

measurement_conditions.why_this_matters: Two earlier runs of this same suite produced numbers that meant nothing. With tmp_path_retention_count = 1, any concurrent pytest deletes the running job's tmp base, and the conductor runs pytest nearly every iteration. The contamination SUPPRESSED the failure count by converting failures into setup errors, so a lower number is not automatically better news.

voided_runs.why_void: tmp base deleted mid-run, worker died, run aborted

supersedes.note: 86 of the July debt was genuinely FIXED, which is why this is a re-baseline rather than a widening. The 1,696 new node ids are NOT all new breakage: roughly 671 are cross-test pollution that passes in isolation. The measurement conditions of the July run are UNKNOWN -- the tmp-deletion hazard existed then too -- so its 116 may itself have been an undercount. Do not read 116 -> 1726 as a pure regression.

known_composition.suite_only_passing_in_isolation: ~671 of the above, across the cwd and triton classes

how_to_use: REQ-HARNESS-5920: readiness may use global_suite_failure_delta<=0 ONLY when every failing node is present here and no new node id appears. This must NOT be used to suppress, deselect, relabel or rewrite unrelated failures.
how_to_shrink: This number should go DOWN. The two suite-only classes are the cheapest wins: they are single root causes, not ~671 independent bugs. Re-baseline downward when they land; never upward without stating what regressed.
